scenes.tts: If two eyes send equal amounts of activity, should they always share a cell?
scenes.visual: Title card: Out of Step. Two equal activity bars, orange and blue. Convention: left hemisphere recorded; right eye (contralateral) orange, left eye (ipsilateral) blue; histograms run group 1 on the left to group 7 on the right.
scenes.narration: If two eyes send equal amounts of activity, should they always share a cell?

scenes.tts: The bookkeeping counts only amount. Strabismus tests whether amount is enough.
scenes.visual: The toy table from the last chapter, with the amount columns highlighted.
scenes.narration: The bookkeeping counts only amount. Strabismus tests whether amount is enough.

scenes.tts: In strabismus the eyes are misaligned. Each points at a different part of the scene.
scenes.visual: Two eyes, one turned; their lines of sight land on different points of a scene.
scenes.narration: In strabismus the eyes are misaligned. Each points at a different part of the scene.

scenes.tts: Hubel and Wiesel produced it in young kittens by cutting one eye muscle.
scenes.visual: Credit: Hubel and Wiesel. A schematic eye with one muscle cut.
scenes.narration: Hubel and Wiesel produced it in young kittens by cutting one eye muscle.

scenes.tts: Each eye still received a normal amount of patterned light.
scenes.visual: Both eyes receive full patterned images. Label: normal amount of light.
scenes.narration: Each eye still received a normal amount of patterned light.

scenes.tts: Predict. Each eye sends about as much activity as in a normal kitten. If amount were all that mattered, what should the histogram look like?
scenes.visual: Question card: each eye sends a normal amount. If amount is all that matters, what histogram shape?
scenes.narration: Predict. Each eye sends about as much activity as in a normal kitten. If amount were all that mattered, what should the histogram look like?

scenes.tts: If amount alone set each cell's split, the histogram would look like a normal one. It did not.
scenes.visual: A normal hump appears, then fades.
scenes.narration: If amount alone set each cell's split, the histogram would look like a normal one. It did not.

scenes.tts: Most cells answered to one eye or the other, and few to both.
scenes.visual: Cells sort to the two ends of the scale.
scenes.narration: Most cells answered to one eye or the other, and few to both.

scenes.tts: The histogram had piles at groups one and seven, and a hollow middle.
scenes.caption: The histogram had piles at groups 1 and 7, and a hollow middle.
scenes.visual: A U-shaped histogram: tall bars at 1 and 7, a hollow middle, the two ends about equal. Schematic.
scenes.narration: The histogram had piles at groups 1 and 7, and a hollow middle.

scenes.tts: Neither eye took over. The cells the two eyes had shared went to one eye or the other. Equal amounts were not enough.
scenes.visual: The two end piles marked balanced; the empty middle labelled lost shared cells.
scenes.narration: Neither eye took over. The cells the two eyes had shared went to one eye or the other. Equal amounts were not enough.

scenes.tts: What changed was not the amount, but the timing between the eyes.
scenes.visual: Label: not amount, timing.
scenes.narration: What changed was not the amount, but the timing between the eyes.

scenes.tts: When the eyes are aligned, they look at the same point.
scenes.visual: Aligned eyes; both lines of sight meet on one point.
scenes.narration: When the eyes are aligned, they look at the same point.

scenes.tts: An edge crossing that point excites both eyes' inputs to a shared cell at nearly the same moments.
scenes.visual: An edge sweeps across the point. Orange and blue spike rasters line up on one shared cell.
scenes.narration: An edge crossing that point excites both eyes' inputs to a shared cell at nearly the same moments.

scenes.tts: Their signals are in step, or correlated.
scenes.visual: Label on the aligned rasters: in step (correlated).
scenes.narration: Their signals are in step, or correlated.

scenes.tts: When the eyes are misaligned, each eye's input arrives while the other is doing something unrelated.
scenes.visual: Misaligned eyes; the orange and blue rasters scatter, no longer lined up.
scenes.narration: When the eyes are misaligned, each eye's input arrives while the other is doing something unrelated.

scenes.tts: A rule that explains this starts with Donald Hebb, in nineteen forty-nine.
scenes.caption: A rule that explains this starts with Donald Hebb, in 1949.
scenes.visual: Credit: Donald Hebb, 1949.
scenes.narration: A rule that explains this starts with Donald Hebb, in 1949.

scenes.tts: Hebb proposed that an input that repeatedly takes part in firing a cell is strengthened.
scenes.visual: An input fires just as the cell fires; that synapse thickens.
scenes.narration: Hebb proposed that an input that repeatedly takes part in firing a cell is strengthened.

scenes.tts: Later models added a weakening half. In the B C M model, an active input weakens when the cell responds, but only weakly.
scenes.caption: Later models added a weakening half. In the BCM model, an active input weakens when the cell responds, but only weakly.
scenes.visual: An input fires while the cell gives only a small response; that synapse thins. Label: added later, BCM model.
scenes.narration: Later models added a weakening half. In the BCM model, an active input weakens when the cell responds, but only weakly.

scenes.tts: An active input strengthens when the cell responds strongly. A silent input changes little.
scenes.visual: A response meter on the cell with a threshold line. Above the line, active synapses thicken; below it, active synapses thin; a silent synapse stays the same.
scenes.narration: An active input strengthens when the cell responds strongly. A silent input changes little.

scenes.tts: The line between strong and weak slides with the cell's recent activity.
scenes.visual: The threshold line rises after a busy spell and falls after a quiet one.
scenes.narration: The line between strong and weak slides with the cell's recent activity.

scenes.tts: Two eyes in step arrive together. The cell responds strongly when both are active, so both are kept.
scenes.visual: Aligned case: both inputs fire together, the response meter goes above the line, and both synapses on the shared cell are kept.
scenes.narration: Two eyes in step arrive together. The cell responds strongly when both are active, so both are kept.

scenes.tts: Out of step, each eye's input often arrives alone. Suppose one eye starts slightly stronger at this cell.
scenes.visual: Misaligned case: the inputs fire at different moments on one cell; the orange synapse is drawn slightly thicker.
scenes.narration: Out of step, each eye's input often arrives alone. Suppose one eye starts slightly stronger at this cell.

scenes.tts: Alone, it drives a strong response and is strengthened. Alone, the other drives only a weak response, and is weakened.
scenes.visual: Orange alone pushes the meter above the line and thickens; blue alone leaves the meter below the line and thins.
scenes.narration: Alone, it drives a strong response and is strengthened. Alone, the other drives only a weak response, and is weakened.

scenes.tts: The lead grows until the cell answers mainly to one eye. Which eye leads differs from cell to cell.
scenes.visual: On one cell orange's lead grows; on a neighbouring cell blue's does. Each cell ends mostly monocular. Label: in a model with a sliding threshold.
scenes.narration: The lead grows until the cell answers mainly to one eye. Which eye leads differs from cell to cell.

scenes.tts: One molecular candidate for detecting together is the N M D A receptor.
scenes.caption: One molecular candidate for detecting together is the NMDA receptor.
scenes.visual: A schematic NMDA receptor in the membrane.
scenes.narration: One molecular candidate for detecting together is the NMDA receptor.

scenes.tts: It passes much current only with glutamate and a co-agonist bound and the cell depolarized enough to clear magnesium from its pore.
scenes.visual: Glutamate and a co-agonist are bound; as the membrane depolarizes, a magnesium ion leaves the pore and current flows.
scenes.narration: It passes much current only with glutamate and a co-agonist bound and the cell depolarized enough to clear magnesium from its pore.

scenes.tts: Now we have both halves of the rule. The cell keeps the eye that helps it fire.
scenes.visual: Rule card: the cell keeps the eye that helps it fire.
scenes.narration: Now we have both halves of the rule. The cell keeps the eye that helps it fire.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: amount matters, but only activity in step with the cell's firing helps an eye keep it.
scenes.visual: Closing card: in step with the cell.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: amount matters, but only activity in step with the cell's firing helps an eye keep it.

scenes.tts: Next, a sharper test: an eye that is silent, against an eye that is noisy.
scenes.visual: Two eyes: one dark, one flickering with scattered spikes.
scenes.narration: Next, a sharper test: an eye that is silent, against an eye that is noisy.
